summary.short: Bill (S. 4591, reported in Senate June 24, 2026) creating a federal property right in individuals' voice and visual likeness, enforceable by civil action against unauthorized digital replicas and related products, with notice-and-takedown safe harbors for online services. Effective 180 days after enactment.
summary.long: S. 4591, reported with an amendment on June 24, 2026, would give each individual and right holder a licensable property right to authorize use of the individual's voice or visual likeness in a 'digital replica' (a newly created, highly realistic computer-generated representation) or in a product or service requiring such authorization. The post-mortem right lasts 10 years, extendable in 5-year periods on proof of active public use, and terminates no later than 70 years after death. Living-person licenses are limited to 10 years and must be written, signed and specific as to uses; minors' licenses are limited to 5 years and need court approval. Anyone who makes available an unauthorized digital replica, or a product primarily designed to produce one, is liable in a civil action, subject to exclusions for news, documentary, commentary, parody and similar uses. Remedies include statutory damages, actual damages and profits, and injunctions. Online services that register a designated agent with the Copyright Office and follow a notice-and-takedown process get a safe harbor. The bill also adds subpoenas to identify violators and preempts most state causes of action with exceptions. It applies to post-enactment conduct and takes effect 180 days after enactment.

notes: Coded from the reported text (Calendar No. 446, reported June 24, 2026, with committee amendment). The introduced text printed with DELETED tags is not coded. No registry instrument is named, so target_instrument_id is empty for all relations. The operative deadlines in Sec. 2(b)(2)(D)(iv) and Sec. 2(d)(2)(C) run from the effective date in Sec. 2(k), 180 days after enactment. The text names no firms; online service providers and designated agents are addressees described by function, not named entities. No internal inconsistencies identified.

enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of subsection (c): unauthorized digital replica activity, or distributing or making available a product or service designed or marketed to produce unauthorized digital replicas
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Greater of: individual $5,000 per work (or per product or service); online service with a good faith effort $25,000 per work (or per product or service); online service without a good faith effort $5,000 per unauthorized display, copy, transmission and instance, capped at $750,000 per work (for products or services, $750,000 per product or service); other entity $25,000 per work (or per product or service); or actual damages plus profits. Punitive damages possible for willful activity; attorney's fees to the prevailing party in specified cases.
enforcement.penalty_formula: Statutory amount per work or per product or service by defendant category, or actual damages plus profits attributable to the use, whichever is greater; cap of $750,000 per work for online services without a good faith effort (no cap stated for products or services); punitive damages for willful activity with malice, fraud, knowledge or willful avoidance of knowledge; attorney's fees to the prevailing party in specified cases.
